A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LQCA study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Pages 2–17 have identical extracted text and rendered content; differences are confined to the first page.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of five LLMs across nine dataset subsets in Table 1, component and sensitivity analyses in Figures 3–5, and coreference perturbation results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, component and sensitivity analyses, and Appendix D perturbation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix G retain the same four-stage LQCA procedure: sub-document coreference resolution, mention-distance computation, representative selection, and mention replacement for question answering.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine subsets of LooGLE, L-Eval, and LongBench, covering summarization and question answering. The positional and perturbation test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Vanilla LM, Zero-shot CoT, RAG with self-Corpus, and RECOMP with self-Corpus. Comparator membership in Figure 3 and Table 2 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same five models, zero-shot evaluation, greedy decoding, truncation policy, coreference threshold, retrieval settings, and ROUGE-L, accuracy, and F1 metrics. Appendix D uses the same perturbation procedure.

E4.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 retain the same component variants, sub-document length and threshold sensitivity analysis, and answer-position analysis. Appendix D retains the experiment randomly perturbing 5% of mentions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Statistical reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, Figures 3–5, and their reported findings are identical. For example, Table 1 gives GPT-4o averages of 63.76 for LQCA and 60.15 for Vanilla LM in both versions.

T1.justification: The definitions and mathematical formulations in Sections 2–3, the proposed causal relationship formula in Appendix E, and the graph algorithm in Appendix G are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain identical claims about LQCA improving long-context understanding through coreference resolution and improved text quality.

C2.justification: The experimental interpretations and future directions are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning ambiguous references, processing overhead for shorter contexts, and adaptability across linguistic structures and domains.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, implementation settings, the Appendix C prompt, Appendix G pseudocode, and the public-code access statement are unchanged. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6, the reference list, and the positioning of LQCA relative to coreference resolution and long-context methods are identical.

P1.justification: v3 removes Shi Bo from the byline, removes the Boston University affiliation and associated email, renumbers the MIT affiliation, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Research prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter affiliation block slightly shifts the abstract, introduction, and Figure 1 upward on page 1. Figure and table content and design are unchanged; pages 2–17 render identically.

improvement.justification: The revision changes author and affiliation information, the version stamp, and first-page spacing. The method, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—remain unchanged, producing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
